evidenceAudit.scope: Women with postpartum haemorrhage (PPH) after vaginal or caesarean birth: prevention, objective diagnosis, the first-response bundle and escalation. Verified against the WHO/FIGO/ICM consolidated PPH guideline (2025) and the Saudi MOH Pocket Manual in Obstetrics & Gynaecology (2014); drug contraindications from US FDA prescribing information.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 12 Oct 2026.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: Saudi MOH manual dated 2014 — check for a newer local protocol
Blood product ratios — local massive transfusion protocol

pathophysiology.summary: PPH is excessive bleeding after birth — primary within 24 h, secondary from 24 h to 12 weeks. The '4 Ts' are tone (uterine atony, about 80%), trauma (cervix, vagina, uterine rupture), tissue (retained placenta) and thrombin (coagulopathy).
keyMechanisms: After placental separation, bleeding from the placental bed is controlled mainly by myometrial contraction compressing spiral arteries ('living ligatures'); atony removes this control.
Uterine blood flow at term is about 600–700 mL/min (stable physiology), so atony can cause massive loss within minutes.
Pregnancy hypervolaemia masks loss: tachycardia and hypotension appear late; shock index above 1 is an early warning.
Massive bleeding consumes and dilutes clotting factors — fibrinogen falls early; coagulopathy (DIC) worsens bleeding.

Risk factors: placental abruption, placenta praevia/accreta, multiple pregnancy, pre-eclampsia, prolonged labour, operative delivery, retained placenta, over-distended uterus, multiparity — but most PPH has no identifiable risk factor (MOH).

symptoms: Heavy vaginal bleeding after birth (may be concealed — intra-abdominal, broad ligament or vaginal haematoma).
physicalSigns: Boggy, poorly contracted uterus above the umbilicus (atony).
Pallor, tachycardia, hypotension, SpO2 below 95%, oliguria (MOH clinical definition).
redFlags: Blood loss 300 mL or more with abnormal vital signs, or 500 mL or more — start the bundle (WHO)
Pulse above 100, shock index above 1, SBP below 100 or DBP below 60 mmHg
Blood loss above 2.5 L — activate the massive blood loss protocol (MOH)
Continued bleeding despite uterotonics — escalate to balloon tamponade or surgery
Bleeding with a well-contracted uterus — look for trauma, haematoma or coagulopathy

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Bleeding with a firm uterus; examine cervix, vagina and perineum.
Severe pain, shock out of proportion; inverted fundus.
Oozing from sites, low fibrinogen and platelets.

clinicalManagement.title: Prevention — third stage of labour
actions: Uterotonic for all births: oxytocin 10 IU IM or IV (WHO first choice), or heat-stable carbetocin 100 µg IM/IV; misoprostol 400–600 µg oral if neither is available.
MOH: oxytocin 5 IU IV or 10 IU IM, with methylergometrine 0.2 mg if no contraindication; controlled cord traction.
Crossmatch blood ready for women with risk factors.
Tranexamic acid is NOT recommended for prevention (WHO).

clinicalManagement.title: First-response bundle (within 15 min of diagnosis)
actions: Call for help: senior obstetrician, anaesthetist, blood bank; one person records times, drugs, fluids and vital signs.
Uterine massage; empty the bladder (Foley catheter).
Oxytocin 10 IU IV slowly over 1–2 min (or in a small volume over 5–10 min), then 10–20 IU infusion over 4 h (WHO). MOH: oxytocin 40 IU in 500 mL Ringer's lactate.
Tranexamic acid 1 g IV over 10 min, within 3 h of birth; repeat 1 g if bleeding continues after 30 min or restarts within 24 h.
Two large-bore IV cannulas; isotonic crystalloid (not colloid); oxygen 10–15 L/min; keep warm.
Examine the genital tract for trauma; check the placenta is complete.

clinicalManagement.title: If bleeding continues — second-line uterotonics
actions: Methylergometrine 0.2 mg IM, repeat as needed (not if hypertensive or pre-eclamptic).
Carboprost 0.25 mg IM every 15 min, maximum 8 doses (2 mg) — not in asthma.
Misoprostol 800 µg sublingual (WHO) or 1000 µg rectal (MOH).
Transfuse early: aim Hb above 8 g/dL, platelets above 75, PT below 1.5× normal, fibrinogen above 1 g/L (MOH).
Activate the massive transfusion protocol; arterial/central lines; ICU.

clinicalManagement.title: Refractory bleeding
actions: Bimanual uterine compression or external aortic compression as a temporising measure.
Uterine balloon tamponade (e.g. Bakri) after excluding retained tissue and trauma.
Retained placenta: manual removal under anaesthesia with prophylactic antibiotics.
Laparotomy: B-Lynch compression suture, uterine then internal iliac artery ligation, embolisation if available; hysterectomy as the last resort (two consultants, family informed — MOH).

clinicalManagement.title: After control
actions: ICU or HDU monitoring; repeat Hb, coagulation, renal function.
Maintenance oxytocin infusion for 4 h.
Thromboprophylaxis once bleeding has stopped (see VTE in pregnancy topic).
Debrief and complete documentation.

keyPoints: Measure blood loss: 300 mL plus abnormal vital signs, or 500 mL = PPH.
Bundle within 15 min: massage, oxytocin, tranexamic acid, fluids, examine, escalate.
Tranexamic acid 1 g IV within 3 h of birth.
No ergometrine in hypertension/pre-eclampsia; no carboprost in asthma.
Escalate early to tamponade, surgery and massive transfusion.
pitfalls: Relying on visual estimation of blood loss.
Giving tranexamic acid after 3 h or as routine prevention.
Missing concealed bleeding or trauma with a contracted uterus.

patientEducation: Explain what happened; iron and anaemia follow-up.

dischargeCriteria: Bleeding controlled, haemodynamically stable, Hb stable and adequate for discharge.
Thromboprophylaxis plan and iron replacement arranged.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Postnatal review of anaemia; debrief the woman; counsel on recurrence risk and plan active management of the third stage in future pregnancies.

values: Objective loss 300 mL + abnormal vital signs, or 500 mL
Symptomatic bleeding; 10% Hb fall; or 500 mL vaginal / 1000 mL caesarean
Oxytocin 10 IU IM/IV (carbetocin or misoprostol alternatives); oxytocin–ergometrine not recommended
Oxytocin 5 IU IV or 10 IU IM with methylergometrine 0.2 mg
1 g IV within 3 h for all PPH, repeat once
Isotonic crystalloids in preference to colloids
Crystalloid 3:1 plus 1–2 L colloid until blood arrives

guidelineComparison.note: Where they differ, follow WHO 2025 (newer evidence: tranexamic acid, crystalloids, objective diagnosis) and confirm with the local protocol.
